key_insight: Crop-level transfer strategies for black-box LVLM attacks induce high-variance, nearly orthogonal gradients (partly due to ViT translation sensitivity). Targeting fine-grained, consistent visual details and reducing gradient variance yields much more stable and effective transfer attacks.
problem_solved: Addresses instability and low transferability of black-box adversarial attacks on Large Vision-Language Models caused by incoherent local alignment and high-variance gradients from crop-level matching.
method: Diagnose source of instability: show ViT translation sensitivity and crop-level matching produce inconsistent gradient directions across iterations.
Fine-grained detail targeting: prioritize consistent patch-/detail-level features instead of coarse crop matches to preserve alignment across updates.
Variance-aware stabilization: incorporate mechanisms to reduce inter-iteration gradient variance and enforce coherent local alignment for more reliable transfer.
impact: Enables more reliable evaluation of LVLM vulnerabilities and guides practitioners toward stronger robustness testing and defense design; highlights the importance of fine-grained alignment when assessing multimodal model security.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: crop-level matching vs fine-grained detail targeting with overlaid gradient vectors showing coherence vs orthogonality.
Line chart: attack success rate / loss vs iterations comparing baseline (M-Attack) and proposed method (stability and faster convergence).
Heatmaps: perturbation or attention maps showing where fine-grained targeting concentrates changes versus diffuse crop-based perturbations.
Pipeline diagram: high-level flow from diagnosis → detail-targeting module → variance stabilization → attack outcome.
paper_title: Pushing the Frontier of Black-Box LVLM Attacks via Fine-Grained Detail Targeting
paper_authors: Xiaohan Zhao, Zhaoyi Li, Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Zhiqiang Shen
